evidence: The CLAUDE.md line genuinely said `usePaneStream(paneId)` while proxy.ts declared `usePaneStream(pane: TmuxPane | null)`; `gh api .../commits/36b71f4` shows CLAUDE.md +1/-1 correcting exactly that line, so the drift was real and the fix was the whole of it.
guidance_note: When a PR changes a seam's signature, edit the doc line that names that seam in the same commit — the doc was rewritten in this PR and still described the old shape.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 36b71f4 touched only CLAUDE.md, PaneViewer.tsx and env.d.ts, not proxy.ts, so this is original PR code. The premise held — 3b34409's diff shows parsePaneList did `(fields[0] ?? '') as PaneId` with no shape check — and the agent's relocation of the fix to the parser (adding `/^%\d+$/` at the cast site) removes the NaN at its source instead of at one of several consumers.
guidance_note: When a parser casts a raw field to a branded type, validate the brand's shape at that cast site so consumers can trust it — the brand is a promise the parser has to earn.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — 36b71f4 did not touch control.ts. Both halves of the premise were real: 2d2589c's message confirms applyWatchedSession `swallowed the owned-session fallback's result` and that TmuxClient.execute reports failure via resp.success rather than throwing, so connect() could reach ready with the client unattached and no %output.
guidance_note: When a wrapper signals failure through a return value instead of an exception, check that value on every call site including the fallback path — an unchecked fallback is a silent dead end.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — 36b71f4 did not touch engine.ts. The 2d2589c patch shows `capture-pane -t ${paneId}` becoming `capture-pane -t ${tmuxEscape(paneId)}`, and kill-pane in the same file already escaped, so the inconsistency the reviewer named was exactly present.
guidance_note: When one call site of a command-string builder escapes its argument, sweep every other site in the same module in the same change rather than leaving the odd one out.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — 3b34409 touched only pane-parse.ts and its test. The premise is confirmed by 035a2cf's own message: the renderer IPC contract declared tmux:watch-session as SessionId|null while the main side had widened back to plain string at watchedSession, watchSession() and the handler.
guidance_note: When a renderer IPC contract declares a branded id, carry the brand through the handler and the main-side field in the same change instead of widening to string on the far side.

evidence: Same defect as F5 seen at a second line; flag is a false positive for the same reason (3b34409 touched pane-parse.ts only). 035a2cf fixed all three sites at once, confirming the reviewer split one gap across four comments.
guidance_note: A brand that is declared on one side of a boundary and widened on the other is a single defect — fix every site the brand crosses in one pass rather than per-comment.

evidence: The IPC handler did take `sessionId: string | null` against a SessionId|null contract; 035a2cf's tmux-control-handlers.ts +2/-1 is the correction. Flag is a false positive — 3b34409 did not touch this file.

Conditional premise (import SessionId if the fields are tightened) that became true once F5-F7 were accepted; 035a2cf's control.ts +3/-2 adds the import. Flag is a false positive — 3b34409 touched pane-parse.ts only.

The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT 035a2cf flag is a false positive (035a2cf did not touch proxy.ts), but the finding is still fix-caused by an earlier one: F3's fix (2d2589c) made applyWatchedSession throw on a failed switch-client, which turned the renderer's pre-existing `void window.electronAPI.invoke(...)` from an inert discard into a live unhandled rejection. f7df5a8's commit message states this directly: `watchSession now throws on a hard switch-client failure` would surface as an unhandled promise rejection. The second half of the finding (redundant switch-client on pane change) is original-PR behaviour, not fix-caused.
guidance_note: When a fix makes a previously non-throwing function throw, grep its callers for discarded promises and unchecked returns in the same change.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT f7df5a8 flag is a false positive (f7df5a8 touched proxy.ts only), but 36b71f4 — the commit the agent named as F1's fix — bundled an unrelated env.d.ts re-brand: its message says the renderer contract `still typed them as plain string` for tmux:pane-processes and re-syncs it to PaneId. That half-sweep left the main-side handler on `string` plus a cast, which is precisely what this finding flags; the mismatch did not exist before that commit.
guidance_note: Do not bundle an unrelated refactor into a commit named as the fix for a review finding — and when re-branding one side of an IPC channel, change the handler on the other side in the same edit.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 177fff7 touched tmux-pane-handlers.ts and env.d.ts, not proxy.ts. The stale-stream window is original-PR behaviour — before f7df5a8 split the effects, the single effect was keyed on [paneId, sessionId] and still set the stream in React state, so the same one-render lag existed. fd04393's message confirms the bug was real: keystrokes during a fast switch could route to the old pane.
guidance_note: State assigned inside an effect lags the render that changed its key — pair derived state with the key it was derived from and gate the read on a match, rather than returning it bare.

narrative: Seven review rounds on a 43-file refactor, and every ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag in the packet is a false positive at the file level — the named fix commits never touched the files the next round flagged. The reviewer simply dribbled findings out of the same unchanged 41-file diff one or two at a time, and four of the eleven findings (F5-F8) are one SessionId branding gap split across four comments. Two findings are genuinely fix-caused and both trace to changes bundled into or made by an earlier fix rather than to an incomplete sweep: F3's fix made watchSession throw and thereby armed an unhandled rejection in the renderer (F9), and the commit named as F1's doc fix quietly re-branded an IPC channel in env.d.ts without updating its handler (F10). The agent's judgment was sound throughout, including its one relocation of a fix from the consumer to the parser (F2), which was the better call.
guidance_observations: Naming a commit as the fix for a finding and then including unrelated refactors in it manufactures the next round's findings — F10 exists only because the F1 doc fix also re-branded env.d.ts.

The agent's claim in F2 that the PaneId brand is now honest everywhere does not cover panes read from persisted commands.json, which the reviewer itself named in F4 as a second, unvalidated producer of PaneId.

Round count here is driven by reviewer incrementality, not by bad fixes: five of seven rounds surfaced findings on code no fix had touched, so guidance aimed at fix completeness would not have shortened this PR.

evidence: The test file newly imports getPaneProcesses, which shells out, while vitest's configured default environment is jsdom; the agent confirms six of eight sibling test files in the same directory already carry the node directive, so the inconsistency was real and local.
guidance_note: When a test file starts exercising OS or child-process APIs, set the environment directive in the same edit that adds the import.

evidence: The added test called `getPaneProcesses(2147483647)` against real pgrep inside a *.test.ts file in a directory that already keeps a .test/.integration.test split; the agent took the reviewer's move option and documented why the mock option failed (module mock did not propagate to the transitive import) and why dep injection would have bypassed isRealExecFailure, the code under test.
guidance_note: A test that shells out to real binaries belongs in the repo's existing .integration.test.ts split from the moment it is written, not after a reviewer names it.

narrative: A small four-file cleanup PR with two low-stakes test-hygiene findings, both correct and both accepted in one round; round 1 produced no comments. Nothing here is fix-caused. The one thing worth keeping is the F2 reply, which is the best-reasoned response in the batch: it names the two alternatives the reviewer offered, reports the experiment it ran against the mock option, and explains why dep injection would have excluded the very code containing the regression.
guidance_observations: Both findings are conventions the repo had already established elsewhere in the same directory (node directive, .integration.test.ts split) — a pre-write check of sibling files in the target directory would have caught both before review.
The F2 reply is the template worth propagating: state which alternatives were considered, what was actually tried, and why the rejected option would have weakened coverage.

evidence: The dead `import type { resolveClientId }` was real and removed, but the reviewer's stated mechanism is doubtful: a genuine `typeof` on a type-only import fails tsc, which would have broken the build before review, and the agent's own word for it is `dangling`. 5c932ef's server.ts change is +2/-2, consistent with deleting a dead import rather than repairing a compile error.
guidance_note: When a refactor swaps one exported helper for another, delete the old import in the same edit instead of demoting it to `import type` and leaving it behind.

evidence: The PR retired tmux:launch-tool, which was the only reader of getClient, leaving the dep in the interface and a comment describing an error path that no longer existed; 5c932ef removes it (tmux-pane-handlers.ts +0/-5, main.ts +0/-1).
guidance_note: When a change removes the last reader of an injected dependency, delete the dep from the interface, the call site, and its explanatory comment in the same change.

evidence: Two comments in spawn.ts contradicted each other in the same function: one justified a has-session pre-check because new-session is unreliable across tmux versions, the other said collision detection is the natural result of new-session so no pre-check is needed. The code has the pre-check, so the second comment was the false one.
guidance_note: When adding a pre-check that supersedes a mechanism a nearby comment already documents, rewrite that comment in the same edit rather than adding a second rationale beside it.

evidence: The file header claimed launch:create and launch:terminate `land in later slices` while the same file registers ipcMain.handle for launch:create; the diff hunk shows both in one screen.
guidance_note: A file header that enumerates what this slice does yet has to be rewritten every time the surface grows — state the surface the file has, never the surface it will have.

evidence: The same PR introduced the LaunchId brand and used it in resolveLaunch, readLaunchHeader and the IPC types, while typing ClientInfo.launchId as plain `string | null`; 5c932ef's proxy-events.ts +8/-1 imports the brand and applies it.
guidance_note: When introducing a branded id, type every field that carries it with the brand in the same commit, shared event and DTO shapes included — a brand with one plain-string hole is not a brand.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 5c932ef's only server.ts change is +2/-2 (F1's dead import), so the frozen lastSeenNs is original-PR behaviour, not fix-caused. The premise is confirmed by the agent's own admission — the previous clientInfoFor helper refreshed the timestamp and `I dropped it when moving to the request-aware resolver and lost this behavior with it`.
guidance_note: When replacing a helper with a new one, enumerate the behaviours the old helper performed and re-implement each — this regression is a dropped side effect, not a missing feature.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — bddc27a touched server.ts only, and registry.ts is original-PR code. `void this.runPersist()` with an injected save() that can reject is a real unhandled-rejection path in the main process; b17bfaa adds the catch plus a test that a later mutation still retries.
guidance_note: Every `void somePromise()` discard needs a rejection handler at the point of the discard — the fire-and-forget is the decision, so the error policy belongs there.

evidence: Flag is a false positive (bddc27a touched server.ts only). The test as written carried its own confession in a comment — `we can't easily mock it here` — while running the real socket-to-pid walk; b17bfaa adds the socketFallback injection point plus a third test asserting the fallback is not called on a header hit.
guidance_note: When a unit test cannot reach a seam, add the injection point rather than shipping the test with a comment apologising for the real I/O it performs.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — b17bfaa touched registry and client-identity, not PaneViewer.tsx. The bug is real: `useLaunchStore((s) => s.byPane)` selects a function defined once in the store creator, so set({launches}) never changes the selected value and the badge never re-renders. fad79f5's patch replaces it with a selector over s.launches. The agent's justification that the result is `structurally compared by Zustand` is wrong — the default comparator is Object.is — but the fix works because setLaunches installs a fresh array from IPC.
guidance_note: Subscribe a store selector to the computed value, never to a lookup function held in store state — a stable function reference silently disables the subscription.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — b17bfaa did not touch main.ts. The comment said slices D/E `will add the exit/recovery wiring` in a block that already wires exit detection and calls recoverLaunches a few lines below.
guidance_note: Comments that promise future slices go stale the moment the slice lands — describe only the behaviour present in the file.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — fad79f5 touched main.ts and PaneViewer.tsx only. listRunning returned every `status !== 'exited'` row including pending, and the reviewer's evidence that the name was misleading is that call sites had already grown `if (launch.status !== 'running') continue` guards to compensate; the rename to listActive is the right resolution of the two offered.
guidance_note: Name a filter after the predicate it applies, not the subset you had in mind — a defensive re-filter at a call site is the signal the name is lying.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — fad79f5 did not touch client-identity.ts. The doc comment promised `Multiple header values resolve to the first non-empty one` while the code read raw[0] and returned null when it was blank; the reviewer offered either direction and the agent picked the stronger one (make the code match the promise), which also removes a real truncation case.
guidance_note: When a doc comment promises behaviour the code lacks, that gap was created by writing the comment first and the code second — decide which is authoritative at write time.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — fad79f5 did not touch registry.ts. The premise is real: create() minted an id when launchId was omitted while the caller supplied an env block that carries PROMPTCTL_LAUNCH_ID, and nothing tied the two. The agent took the reviewer's second option; 106812b's guard is `envId !== undefined && envId !== launchId`, so a row whose env simply omits the var still slips through — a weaker fix than making launchId required, which the reviewer also offered.
guidance_note: When a reviewer offers a type-level fix and a runtime-check fix for the same invariant, do not pick the runtime check to preserve a test convenience — the injected id factory does not require the public field to be optional.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — fad79f5 did not touch recovery.ts. The header narrated a pipeline (`resolve pid, inspect env, registry.attach or markExited`) whose attach step the implementation never performs; the agent confirmed recovery only verifies the already-persisted pid.
guidance_note: When a module header narrates a pipeline step by step, check each named step exists in the code before committing the header — this batch has four of these.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — fad79f5 did not touch correlator.ts. The header listed three subscription channels while startLaunchCorrelator wires two, and a note lower in the same file said explicitly that server-death is not a trigger, so the file contradicted itself.

Flag is a false positive — 106812b touched correlator, recovery, registry and client-identity, not shared/types.ts. The comment enumerated three injected env keys while launchEnvBlock injects four; the reviewer's cross-check was the tests that assert PROMPTCTL_LAUNCH_TOOL.
guidance_note: A comment that enumerates a set produced elsewhere in the code is a second source of truth for that set — point at the producer instead of listing its members.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — 106812b did not touch Live.tsx or Live.test.tsx. The PR added a conditional marker with its own data-testid and no assertion on either branch; 4aecc37's Live.test.tsx +21/-0 is the missing coverage.
guidance_note: New conditional UI ships with the test that asserts both branches — adding a data-testid without an assertion is coverage theatre.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — 106812b did not touch correlator.test.ts. The harness's fake onTopologySnapshot only pushed the listener, while the production TmuxTopologyTracker.onSnapshot invokes it synchronously with the current snapshot, so the whole initial-reconcile path was untested; note the same synchronous-attach contract is what F28 later leaks against.
guidance_note: A hand-written fake for a subscription API must reproduce the real API's synchronous-first-callback behaviour, or every bug in the boot path is invisible to the suite.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — 4aecc37 touched correlator.test.ts, Live.test.tsx and types.ts. The premise is real and paired with F20: subscribers only shrank on WebContents destruction, while the renderer handed callers an unsubscribe function that did nothing to main. 3d92f66 adds the launch:unsubscribe channel.
guidance_note: When a subscribe path hands the caller an unsubscribe handle, implement the channel that actually unsubscribes — an unsubscribe that only detaches local listeners is a false contract.

evidence: The renderer half of F19's defect, on the same commit and fixed by the same 3d92f66; flag is a false positive for the same reason. initLaunchSubscription's returned cleanup removed only unsubList/unsubEvents and never told main to drop the sender.

Flag is a false positive — 3d92f66 touched launch-handlers.ts, env.d.ts and store/launches.ts, not recovery.ts. `await readPidEnv(launch.pid).catch(() => null)` collapsed ps-missing, EACCES and transient I/O into the same value that means process-gone, and the next branch marked the row exited — so a readable failure orphaned a live tool. The agent agreed and named its own law.
guidance_note: A `.catch(() => sentinel)` collapses every error into one meaning — catch the specific expected condition by its code and let everything else throw.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — f810ad3 touched recovery.ts and its test only; the socket cache is original-PR code. The inconsistency is real (the cache held header-derived identity, so the first request on a keep-alive connection fixed it forever) but the reviewer's scenario is close to unreachable in production: the header comes from ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS baked into the launch env once at spawn, so it does not change mid-connection. This partly-theoretical finding is the most expensive one in the packet — its fix produced F24, F25 and, one round later, F32.
guidance_note: When a finding says read the cheap input per request and cache only the expensive part, implement it inside the existing resolver rather than inlining a second copy at the call site.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — f810ad3 did not touch store/launches.ts. The comment claimed the store is populated `before any consumer renders`, but initLaunchSubscription is awaited from App's useEffect, which runs after the first paint; the agent conceded the seed only removes a repaint.
guidance_note: Do not write a guarantee into a comment that the call site's lifecycle cannot provide — check where the function is invoked from before describing when its effects land.

evidence: Directly fix-caused and verified: 1b9f429 (the F22 fix) changed handleRequest to read the header per request and cache only the socket walk, but left the block comment above the server saying the first request `resolves identity ... and caches the result` and that `the header is stable across a connection's lifetime`. f197832's diff shows that exact comment being replaced, confirming the fix stranded it.
guidance_note: When a fix changes caching or resolution semantics, grep the same file for the comment that states the old semantics and rewrite it in the same commit.

evidence: Verified against 1b9f429's patch: it deleted the `resolveRequestClient(req, req.socket, resolveLaunch)` call and replaced it with an inlined readLaunchHeader / resolveLaunch / clientInfoFromLaunch / resolveClientId block, creating a second implementation of the identity resolver that the client-identity tests do not cover. The F22 fix broke the single-resolver property that existed before it.
guidance_note: Fix a caching problem by injecting the cache into the existing resolver, not by re-implementing the resolver at the call site — the tested path and the production path must stay the same code.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — 1b9f429 touched server.ts and store/launches.ts, not App.tsx. The race is real and pre-dates the launch work: initCommandSubscription already used the same store-the-unsubscribe-after-await shape, and the PR copied it for initLaunchSubscription; the agent conceded it missed the pattern on the first pass.
guidance_note: An effect that awaits before storing its unsubscribe needs a disposed flag set by the cleanup and checked when the promise resolves — copying an existing effect copies its bugs too.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — f197832 touched server.ts and App.tsx, not store/launches.ts. The `(...args)` plus `args[0] as Launch[]` pattern does defeat the typed ElectronAPI.on overloads the same PR added in env.d.ts, and the two sibling init functions in the codebase already used named params.
guidance_note: When the project ships typed IPC overloads, take the payload as a named parameter — a variadic signature plus a cast silently opts out of the checking the overload exists to provide.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — 07c6084 touched store/launches.ts only; spawn.ts is original-PR code. The leak is real and the agent confirmed the mechanism: the topology adds the listener to its set after the synchronous first callback, so a promise settled during that callback left `unsubscribe` null and stop() a no-op — one leaked listener per spawn. Notably the comment above the function already reasoned about that synchronous window, but only about the TDZ it caused.
guidance_note: When a subscribe API calls back synchronously on attach, handle the settled-before-the-handle-exists case explicitly — the mutable-holder trick fixes the TDZ and hides the leak behind it.

evidence: Fix-caused and verified: f810ad3 (the F21 fix) rewrote recoverLaunches to mean null-is-gone and throw-is-investigate, and the agent's F21 reply asserted null was the `genuine process gone` signal from readEnvMacos and readEnvLinux — but readEnvLinux still mapped EACCES to null, so the new contract was false for the Linux producer. ba7eab4 fixes readEnvLinux itself.
guidance_note: When a fix makes a caller depend on null-means-X and throw-means-Y, audit every producer of that null in the same change — the caller's contract is only as true as its weakest producer.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — ba7eab4 touched recovery.ts and spawn.ts, not persistence.ts. The reviewer's strongest point is that the code contradicted its own adjacent comment: the comment said we would rather lose the cache than silently coerce, while the code did `return parsed as Launch[]` after only an isArray check, letting rows missing status or launchId into a discriminated union the correlator switches on.
guidance_note: A comment stating a validation policy is not the validation — when persisting a discriminated union, validate the discriminator and its state-specific fields per row at load.

evidence: Flag is a false positive — 185cfa0 touched persistence.ts and its test only, and the `event.sender.once('destroyed', ...)` line is original launch-handlers.ts code (3d92f66's later edit was +11/-0 adding the unsubscribe handler beside it). The defect is real regardless: Set.add is idempotent and once() is not, so any repeat subscribe from one WebContents stacks handlers. Worth noting the reviewer's stated trigger, subscribe/unsubscribe cycles, only became routine because of the F19 and F20 fix — but the code it flags predates that fix.
guidance_note: Register a one-shot lifecycle listener behind the same membership check that makes the registration idempotent — reasoning that Set.add is idempotent does not transfer to the listener added next to it.

evidence: Fix-caused and verified: f197832 (the F25 fix) introduced `const cachedFallback = (sock: net.Socket) => { const existing = socket[CLIENT_INFO]; ... }`, reading and writing the closed-over `socket` while taking `sock` as a parameter. The reviewer scoped it honestly as a latent foot-gun rather than a live bug, which is right — the two are the same object today.
guidance_note: A closure whose parameter shadows an in-scope variable must use the parameter throughout, or take no parameter at all — half-using it is the shape that survives review and breaks on the next refactor.

narrative: Fifteen rounds on a +3574/-120 PR, with 32 findings the agent accepted essentially all of. Four are genuinely fix-caused, and they cluster on two fixes: F22's per-request-header rewrite stranded the comment describing the old caching semantics (F24) and inlined a second copy of the identity resolver (F25), whose own fix then wrote a closure that ignores its parameter (F32); separately, F21's fix declared a null-means-gone contract that readEnvLinux did not honour (F29). Every other ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive at the file level — the named commit did not touch the flagged file. The dominant cost is not fix quality but the original PR: nine of the 32 findings are comments contradicting the code they sit above, a direct consequence of writing long law-citing block comments and then changing the code beneath them. Rounds 9, 11 and 13 each carried a fix-caused finding, though each also carried an independent one, so eliminating the fix-caused findings would have shortened those rounds rather than removing them.
guidance_observations: Nine of 32 findings (F3, F4, F10, F12, F14, F15, F16, F23, F24) are narrative comments contradicting adjacent code — the practice of writing multi-paragraph [LAW:...] block comments that enumerate channels, pipeline steps, env keys and future slices generates a review finding every time the code moves under them.

Two findings (F22, F25) show the same anti-pattern in the fix itself: accepting a finding about a call site by inlining logic at that call site instead of pushing the change into the function that already owns the decision.

The reviewer offered two options on five findings (F2, F11, F12, F13, F30) and the agent picked the weaker one only on F13, where a runtime check was kept over a required field to preserve a test convenience — worth a rule that test ergonomics never justify keeping an illegal state representable.

F18 and F28 are the same underlying fact — a subscription API that calls back synchronously on attach — found four rounds apart in a fake and in production code; a single sweep of the onSnapshot contract's call sites would have caught both at once.
